writing.prompt: Directions: Suppose it is proposed that university students should be required to participate in at least one research project. You are now to write a response by stating what you think of the proposal in terms of its necessity and practicality. You will have 30 minutes to write the response. You should write at least 120 words but not more than 180 words.
writing.sample: Requiring university students to take part in at least one research project is a proposal worth supporting, provided it is implemented flexibly and students can choose topics that interest them. From my perspective, such a policy is both necessary and practical for most undergraduates.First, it is necessary because research experience bridges the gap between textbook knowledge and real-world problem solving. Through a well-designed project, students learn to ask meaningful questions, collect reliable data, and think critically. These abilities are essential for their future careers. Second, it is practical because universities already have laboratories, supervisors, and course projects in place. A single semester-long project can fit into the existing curriculum without placing too much burden on students.Therefore, I support the proposal. It helps students develop practical skills that lectures alone cannot provide, and its flexible design makes it achievable for most universities.

transcript.en: A man was left with a $1,000 bill, after his 6-year-old son ordered a virtual buffet of food from several restaurants last weekend. This led to a string of unexpected deliveries, and maybe a starring role in an advertisement campaign.
transcript.zh: 上周末，一名男子的6岁儿子从多家餐厅订购了一顿“虚拟自助餐”，结果给他留下了一张1000美元的账单。这引发了一连串意外送餐，也可能让他在一场广告宣传活动中担任主角。

transcript.en: Keith Stonehouse said the food piled up quickly at his home Saturday night, after he let his son use his cell phone to play a game before bed. He said the youngster instead used his father's online food ordering account to order food from one restaurant after another. The boy's mother, Christine Stonehouse, said that the online food app has reached out to the family and offered them a $1,000 gift card. The company also is considering using the family in an online promotional campaign.
transcript.zh: 基思·斯通豪斯说，上周六晚上，他让儿子睡前用自己的手机玩游戏，之后食物很快就堆满了家里。他说，孩子没有玩游戏，而是使用父亲的在线点餐账户，一家接一家地订购食物。男孩的母亲克里斯蒂娜·斯通豪斯说，这款在线点餐应用已经联系了他们一家，并向他们提供了一张价值1000美元的礼品卡。该公司还在考虑让这一家人参与一场线上宣传活动。

transcript.en: Most of the food went into the family's refrigerators. They also invited some neighbors over to eat some of it. The father is planning to change his password.
transcript.zh: 大部分食物都放进了家里的冰箱。他们还邀请了一些邻居来吃掉其中一部分。孩子的父亲打算更改密码。

transcript.en: Animal behaviour experts looked at more than 100 research papers. They examined how visitors affected the behaviour of more than 250 species in zoos. They found that elephants socialised more with each other during public feeding times. After public feeding times, they were more likely to search for food and less likely to be inactive. In the presence of many visitors, elephants were less likely to use repetitive behaviours which often indicate boredom.
transcript.zh: 动物行为专家查阅了100多篇研究论文。他们研究了参观者如何影响动物园中250多种动物的行为。他们发现，在面向公众的喂食时段，大象彼此之间的社交活动更多。公众喂食时段结束后，大象更有可能寻找食物，也不太可能处于不活动状态。在众多参观者在场时，大象较少表现出重复性行为，而这类行为通常表明它们感到无聊。

transcript.en: Visitors had a similar effect on some other species too, including polar bears, certain jungle cats and black-tailed plain dogs. Some animal species have been born and raised in zoos, and so have likely become used to the presence of humans. Zoo visitors are often aspects of a zoo animal's environment that animals cannot control, and as such can be stressful, although some species appear to show good adaptability to the changing conditions of visitors.
transcript.zh: 参观者对其他一些物种也产生了类似影响，包括北极熊、某些丛林猫科动物和黑尾草原犬。一些动物物种出生并成长于动物园，因此很可能已经习惯了人类的存在。对动物园里的动物而言，参观者通常是其环境中动物无法控制的因素，因此可能会造成压力，尽管有些物种似乎表现出对参观者状况变化的良好适应能力。

transcript.en: Denver is suspending its popular electric bike incentive program. The program was launched in April. It allowed Denver residents to apply for $400 in government funds before buying an electric bike from a participating shop. Residents who met certain income qualifications could qualify for $1,200. More than 3,000 Denver residents applied for incentives within the first 3 weeks.
transcript.zh: 丹佛暂停了广受欢迎的电动自行车激励计划。该计划于4月启动，允许丹佛居民在从参与计划的商店购买电动自行车之前，申请400美元的政府补助。符合特定收入条件的居民可获得1,200美元。启动后的前3周内，超过3,000名丹佛居民申请了补助。

transcript.en: The city then changed the program to limit the number of applications each month. On Monday, the city announced the pause. "We're honored to be a part of transforming the way Denver wants to move around," said Grace Rink, Denver's chief climate officer. "We exhausted three years' worth of funding in six months." The city said the program has put 4,400 electric bikes on the streets of Denver and invested $8.6 million into the local economy. The city has provided 2,200 incentives to lower-income residents that represent 68% of the program funding. The city expects to resume the program early next year. It also plans design changes to make participation easier and increase access to the program.
transcript.zh: 随后，该市对计划进行了调整，限制每月的申请数量。周一，该市宣布暂停该计划。丹佛首席气候官格蕾丝·林克说：“我们很荣幸能够参与改变丹佛人出行的方式。”她说：“我们在6个月内用尽了原本可供3年使用的资金。”该市表示，这项计划已让4,400辆电动自行车行驶在丹佛街头，并向当地经济投入了860万美元。该市已向低收入居民提供2,200项补助，占计划资金的68%。该市预计明年年初恢复该计划，同时还计划进行设计调整，以便居民更容易参与并扩大计划的覆盖范围。

transcript.en: W: Hey, Mike, what do you think of the museum you visited today?
transcript.zh: W: 嘿，迈克，你觉得今天参观的博物馆怎么样？

transcript.en: M: Hey, Sue. The museum is great, very interesting. They have loads of stuff there on display. The primitive tools early humans used tell a lot about their life, but my favorite is the coin collection. They have some coins that are over 2,000 years old.
transcript.zh: M: 嘿，苏。这个博物馆很棒，非常有意思。那里展出了很多东西。早期人类使用的原始工具能让我们了解到很多他们的生活情况，不过我最喜欢的是钱币收藏。他们有些钱币已经有两千多年的历史了。

transcript.en: W: That sounds cool.
transcript.zh: W: 听起来很酷。

transcript.en: M: Yeah, what did you do today?
transcript.zh: M: 是啊，你今天做了什么？

transcript.en: W: Kathy and I just wandered through the old city centre. The streets are narrow but beautiful with plenty of charm. We saw the Trevi Fountain, which is in all the guidebooks.
transcript.zh: W: 我和凯西只是逛了逛老城区。街道虽然狭窄，却很漂亮，充满了魅力。我们看了特莱维喷泉，所有旅游指南上都有介绍。

transcript.en: M: How do you like it?
transcript.zh: M: 你觉得怎么样？

transcript.en: W: It's very pretty, but it was overcrowded with tourists.
transcript.zh: W: 非常漂亮，不过游客太多了，挤得水泄不通。

transcript.en: M: Yeah, well, it's crowded everywhere. It is August after all, the busiest month of the year.
transcript.zh: M: 是啊，到处都很拥挤。毕竟现在是八月，一年中最繁忙的月份。

transcript.en: W: Yes, it's like the whole world is here on holiday, including us. What will you do tomorrow?
transcript.zh: W: 是啊，感觉全世界的人都来这里度假了，包括我们。你明天打算做什么？

transcript.en: M: I haven't decided yet. I was thinking of doing what you did today—wandering the old streets and taking pictures. I was also thinking of visiting the square with the Spanish steps.
transcript.zh: M: 我还没决定。我在考虑做你今天做的事，逛逛老街，拍拍照。我还在考虑去看看有西班牙阶梯的那个广场。

transcript.en: W: What is that? I haven't heard of it.
transcript.zh: W: 那是什么地方？我没听说过。

transcript.en: M: It's a square where on one side, there are some very wide steps with flowers that go up to a church. It's also in all the tourist guidebooks. It's very famous and pretty. I was also thinking of seeing that tomorrow.
transcript.zh: M: 那是一个广场，广场一侧有一段很宽的台阶，台阶上摆满了鲜花，一直通向一座教堂。旅游指南上也都有介绍。那里非常有名，也很漂亮。我也在考虑明天去看看。

transcript.en: W: It sounds very nice. Do you mind if Kathy and I join you tomorrow?
transcript.zh: W: 听起来很不错。你介意明天我和凯西跟你一起去吗？

transcript.en: M: Not at all. I spent the whole day today pretty much alone. Doing tourist stuff with others would be a welcome change.
transcript.zh: M: 当然不介意。我今天基本上独自待了一整天。和别人一起做些游客会做的事，换换方式也挺不错的。

transcript.en: W: Let me ask her first, but I'm sure she'll be up for it.
transcript.zh: W: 我先问问她，不过我相信她会愿意去的。

transcript.en: W: Sure. It's important not to undermine the significance of the first few days of your job, since this is the best time to create a solid first impression.

transcript.en: W: That's right. And in that respect, it's also important to learn about the business to see the big picture.

transcript.en: M: You mean like knowing about the history of the company.

transcript.en: W: Kind of, but more like knowing the details of the products and services that the company exists to deliver. Learning about the business will give you a chance to understand how your role fits into the bigger picture.
transcript.zh: W: 算是吧，不过更重要的是了解公司赖以存在的那些产品和服务的具体情况。了解公司业务能让你明白自己的职责是如何融入更大的整体的。

transcript.en: Contrary to popular belief, consumers aren't as smart as they like to believe. Many consumers report comparing multiple competing brands and prices when evaluating a purchase. However, research indicates that this is not actually the case. What consumers really think or feel often contradicts what they say. A big reason is that they are driven by unconscious urges, the biggest of which is emotion.
transcript.zh: 与普遍看法相反，消费者并没有他们自认为的那么聪明。许多消费者表示，在评估一项购买时，他们会比较多个相互竞争的品牌及其价格。然而，研究表明，实际情况并非如此。消费者真正的想法或感受往往与他们所说的相矛盾。一个重要原因是，他们受到无意识冲动的驱使，其中最主要的就是情感。

transcript.en: Emotion is what really drives the purchasing behaviors, and also, decision making in general. Good marketers keep in mind this important fact all the time, and examples of emotion-based campaigns are everywhere. Think for a moment, what is actually being sold in most marketing campaigns? Luxury goods target our feelings of self-worth, acceptance, and status in the world. Communication devices excite us by offering a connection to friends, family and a broader network of people. And many other products, such as rings, target emotions related to love and relationships.
transcript.zh: 真正驱动购买行为的，是情感；一般而言，决策也是如此。优秀的营销人员始终牢记这一重要事实，而以情感为基础的营销活动随处可见。请想一想，大多数营销活动实际上销售的是什么？奢侈品瞄准的是我们关于自我价值、认同感以及社会地位的感受。通信设备通过提供与朋友、家人以及更广泛人际网络的联系，使我们感到兴奋。许多其他产品，例如戒指，则瞄准与爱情和人际关系相关的情感。

transcript.en: As marketers, we should focus on the features of the product, but we must also sell the lifestyle and the feeling. The key is to highlight the emotional response a consumer will have by using the product. To achieve the highest emotional response, we should target our consumer through many different senses. A lot of what drives consumers is subconscious behavior. But this isn't a bad thing. There's nothing manipulative about helping consumers achieve desired states of emotion.
transcript.zh: 作为营销人员，我们应当关注产品的功能，但也必须销售一种生活方式和一种感受。关键在于突出消费者使用产品后将产生的情感反应。为了达到最强烈的情感反应，我们应当通过许多不同的感官来触达消费者。驱动消费者行为的诸多因素都属于潜意识行为。但这并不是一件坏事。帮助消费者获得期望的情感状态，并没有任何操纵性。

transcript.en: Plastics have for years been used to make nearly everything that surrounds us. But along the way, they escaped the confines of packaging and objects and settled in the environment, the food we eat and the air we breathe.
transcript.zh: 多年来，塑料一直被用于制造我们周围几乎所有的东西。但在这一过程中，它们逃离了包装和物品的束缚，进入了环境、我们所吃的食物以及所呼吸的空气中。

transcript.en: Americans are consuming and breathing in a lot of plastic. Based on available data, Americans take in an estimated 74,000 to 121,000 microplastic particles every year. However, scientists believe the true number is probably much higher, because for some likely sources of microplastics, there were no strong data available.
transcript.zh: 美国人正在摄入并吸入大量塑料。根据现有数据估算，美国人每年摄入的微塑料颗粒数量在7.4万至12.1万之间。然而，科学家认为真实数量可能高得多，因为对于一些很可能的微塑料来源，目前没有可靠的数据。

transcript.en: Microplastics get into food and air in several ways. Many start off as part of larger plastic objects, which over time fragment into smaller and smaller pieces until they become tiny: 5 millimeters or less in diameter. They are breathed in or consumed by animals, and then become our food. The particles float through the air until people breathe them in. They also settle on the food that people eat.
transcript.zh: 微塑料通过多种方式进入食物和空气。许多微塑料最初是较大塑料物品的一部分，随着时间的推移逐渐碎裂成越来越小的碎片，最终变得十分微小，直径仅为5毫米或更小。它们会被动物吸入或摄入，随后成为我们的食物。这些颗粒漂浮在空气中，直到人们将其吸入。它们也会沉积在供人们食用的食物上。

transcript.en: Data shows that for Americans, air, bottled water and seafood were the biggest sources for breathed-in or consumed microplastics. Added sugars accounted for less, and salts, tap water and beer contributed minimal amounts. These estimates are conservative. The included foods only make up about 15% of the average American diet. It's not yet known how much plastic is contained in the remaining 85% of the typical diet.
transcript.zh: 数据显示，对于美国人来说，空气、瓶装水和海鲜是吸入或摄入微塑料的最大来源。添加糖所占比例较小，而盐、自来水和啤酒所贡献的数量极少。这些估算是保守的。所纳入的食物仅约占美国人平均饮食的15%。典型饮食中剩余的85%含有多少塑料，目前尚不清楚。

transcript.en: People looking to stay well as they age may want to adopt a pet animal, according to new data from the University of Michigan National Poll on Healthy Aging. For the survey, researchers polled about 2,000 U.S. adults from ages 50 to 80. 55% said they owned at least one pet. Dogs were the most common pet, followed by cats. But whatever the type of animal, the vast majority of owners said their pets boosted their mental and physical health.
transcript.zh: 密歇根大学健康老龄化全国民意调查的最新数据显示，希望随着年龄增长保持健康的人或许可以考虑养一只宠物。调查中，研究人员询问了约2,000名年龄在50至80岁之间的美国成年人。55%的人表示自己至少养有一只宠物。狗是最常见的宠物，其次是猫。但无论饲养何种动物，绝大多数宠物主人都表示，宠物改善了他们的心理和身体健康。

transcript.en: Nearly 90% of older pet owners said their animals helped them enjoy life and feel loved; roughly 80% said their pets reduced stress; and almost three-quarters said their pets provided a sense of purpose. However, people did report a few disadvantages to pet ownership. This included difficulty traveling and financial strains. 6% of pet owners said they'd fallen or injured themselves as a result of having a pet.
transcript.zh: 近90%的老年宠物主人表示，宠物帮助他们享受生活并感受到关爱；约80%的人表示，宠物减轻了他们的压力；近四分之三的人表示，宠物让他们感到生活有目标。不过，人们确实也报告了养宠物带来的一些不利之处，包括出行困难和经济压力。6%的宠物主人表示，他们曾因养宠物而跌倒或受伤。

transcript.en: Still, plenty of research has shown that just about anyone can benefit from their pet, since animals can lower stress, reduce symptoms of depression and anxiety and encourage physical activity. The new poll suggests that pet ownership may be especially beneficial for older adults, given how common loneliness and social isolation are within this age group. Human social support comes with a host of health benefits—less stress, lower rates of long-term disease and more—and research shows that interacting with pets can bring many of the same benefits.
transcript.zh: 尽管如此，大量研究表明，几乎所有人都能从宠物身上受益，因为动物能够减轻压力，缓解抑郁和焦虑症状，并促进身体活动。这项新的民意调查表明，养宠物对老年人可能尤其有益，因为孤独和社会隔离在这一年龄群体中十分普遍。人类的社会支持能够带来一系列健康益处，包括减轻压力、降低长期疾病的发生率等；研究表明，与宠物互动也能带来许多相同的益处。

matching.title: The Star Quality of New Zealand's Great Barrier Island

paragraphs.t: I was glad I had such terrible jetlag. Wide awake at 3:30 am with our nine-year-old daughter on our lodge balcony, I stared for hours at the most incredible night sky I've ever seen before the dawn slowly started to rub out the stars on the horizon and the multiple shooting stars faded away.

We were going to my wife's big family reunion in Auckland, New Zealand, but when we found out that Great Barrier Island, just off the coast, had been recently awarded Dark Sky Sanctuary status—a typically remote area that has an "exceptional or distinguished quality of starry nights"—we thought it would be the perfect place to relax before our busy schedule. It's the first island and only the fourth location in the world to achieve this status.

After a 28-hour flight with two travel-sick children, our hearts sank when we saw the tiny twin engine 10- seater that was to take us the 90km across the Hauraki Gulf to Great Barrier Island. But we needn't have worried. Whether it was the gravity force of the plane climbing or the noise of the engine, it put our three- year-old daughter instantly to sleep until we bumped down on the grass at Claris Airport. Our first empty sick bag against all the odds…Things were looking up.

Great Barrier Island has no public facilities and the 950 people living there (though only about half permanently) rely on solar and wind energy, and bottled gas for cooking. There are no streetlights. There are no cash machines or banks. The police force comprises a husband and wife, and there's one postman. It's not just the lack of light but the lack of noise that's so delightful on this unique and gorgeous scene. It was first discovered by East Polynesians about 700 years ago and the Maori name for the island is Aotea. Captain Cook gave the island its European name, because it acts as a barrier between the Pacific and the Hauraki Gulf.

The climate here is subtropical(亚热带的) like Auckland's. The island boasts a beautiful wilderness with dense forests, glorious, unspoilt sandy beaches and plenty of bays and a few mountainous areas where there are good walking tracks among the wetlands and valleys. You can birdwatch, dive, surf and boat. The best beaches are on the eastern side of the island where the surf is better, too. The sheltered western side is where you'll find the best diving and boating. Lots of people come here for the fantastic fishing spots around the island. Like a lot of spots in New Zealand, there are whale-watching trips and you might just catch sight of sharks.

It's rare to find an island that really does feel undiscovered—but this is it. When one of my wife's relations, who comes here regularly, found out that we'd been there, he whispered to us, only half-joking: "Shh—don't tell anyone!" The locals are a relaxed and friendly bunch—a lot of them told us that it's like what Waiheke Island (now in effect a suburb of Auckland) was in the 1970s when it was a commune of artists and people wanting to escape the city.

Our guide for some of our stay was the inestimable Hilde Hoven, a Dark Sky ambassador who runs Good Heavens with Deborah Kilgallon and Orla Cumisky. They bring their Dobsonian telescope and beanbags (it's hard work staring up wide-eyed in wonder without neck support) and, our elder daughter was glad to hear, hot chocolate to wherever you are on the island. "It's odd but when the light readings were done," said Hilde, explaining how the island was awarded its special status, "they found there was more light pollution on the northern side coming from Fiji, which is about 3,000km away, than Auckland to the south. It's pretty dark!"

Beginning their astronomical PowerPoint demonstration using a green laser pointer, Hilde and Orla showed us the Messier 4 spherical cluster(星团) with white dwarf stars(白矮星), Saturn and its rings, the Southern Cross and the Milky Way, which stretched across the sky. Our daughter was especially taken with Hilde's narrating of the Maori myth of Māui's fish hook to explain the shape of Scorpius. In the fable, Māui hauled the North Island of New Zealand from the bottom of the ocean with his hook.

We stayed at Mount St Paul's Estate, a luxurious lodge run by the friendly Chris and Teara, both from Canada. Teara used to be a chef at the Langham in Auckland and so dinner, eaten around a huge circular table (made of one of the most ancient trees in the world), was every bit as mouth-watering as you'd expect. Eating pancakes on the balcony overlooking the unspoilt white sandy beach was a great way to start the day.

Another highlight was an hour-long walk to Kaitoke hot pools in the centre of the island, through wetlands and a forest, where we whiled away a good hour sitting in the pools shaded from the heat by layers of delicate umbrella-like plants.

We also loved visiting the potter(陶艺家) Sarah Harrison, who showed us round her studio at Shoal Bay harbour, and her many pots and jugs, plates and bowls and colourful mosaics(马赛克). In her work, she also uses a lot of materials found on the beach. Our elder daughter loved the gorgeous hidden pool at Medlands beach where the water is separated from the sea in a private rock pool. Other high points were the ancient pōhutukawa trees and the incredible views of Okiwi Basin and Whangapoua beach from the top of Windy Canyon, just a 10-minute hike through a narrow valley up some steep wooden steps on the eastern side of the island.

Apparently the island council turned down famous musician Paul McCartney's application to buy a property at Great Barrier Island because of the unwelcome attention he would have brought. You can see why he wanted to come here; equally, the island knows exactly what kind of star watching it prefers.

questions.s: The author's daughter slept throughout the last leg of their flight to Great Barrier Island.

careful.passage: Is organic food worth the higher price? It's the classic grocery store dilemma. On the one hand, your family dinner table deserves only the best. On the other hand, your wallet can only stretch so far. Whether or not to buy organic is a personal decision, said Mike von Massow, professor of Food Agriculture. Science won't give a clear-cut answer to the question of whether organic food is "better". There are often trade-offs(权衡) and answers become less definitive depending on the product under consideration. One thing is definitive: Organic and conventionally grown food are equally nutritious. From a nutrition point of view, there is no difference between organic and traditionally grown products. Organic products don't necessarily have fewer pesticides(杀虫剂)—in fact, they may have more. There is also no big difference between organic and non-organic products from a food-safety perspective. Even organic growers use pesticides. Testing shows little if any pesticide remains on conventionally grown products. In fact, organic farmers often use larger quantities of pesticide because they can only use the natural variety of insect-killers. Chemical pesticides generally kill a much wider range of pests(害虫) than any single natural pesticide. The use of animal waste in organic agriculture can also be a factor in the spread of bacteria like E. coli and salmonella. Over the past 10 years, Canada has seen more food-safety recalls for organic products, proportionally, than for conventional products. On the whole, organic agriculture may have a smaller environmental footprint. That's mostly because the risk of groundwater contamination from organic farming is lower. Organic farmers never use neonics, the controversial pesticides that have been linked to shrinking bee populations worldwide. Traditional agriculture has been making "dramatic improvements" to reduce its impact on the environment. It isn't a black-and-white picture, though. Organic farming is much less efficient when it comes to land use, although yields vary considerably depending on the crop. On the other hand, advocates of organic farming argue yields and efficiency could be significantly improved if the food industry devoted as much research and money to organic farming as it does conventional agriculture.

careful.passage: It is still controversial whether we are fundamentally generous or selfish and whether these tendencies are shaped by our genes or environment. Some evidence points to humans being born cooperative. At later stages in life we routinely work together to reach goals and help out in times of need. Yet instances of selfish behavior are also plenty. One recent study tested people's willingness to set aside selfish interests to reach a greater good. It found that being selfish was more advantageous than cooperating. The benefit may be short-lived, however. Another study showed that players who cooperated did better in the long run. It seems that human nature supports both pro-social and selfish traits(特征). Genetic studies have made some progress toward identifying their biological roots. By comparing identical twins, who share nearly 100 percent of their genes, and non-identical twins, who share about half, researchers have found overwhelming evidence for genetic effects on behaviors. In these twin studies, identical and non-identical twins are asked, for example, to split a sum of money with a peer. Such studies often also rely on careful psychological assessments and DNA analysis. Other work highlights specific genes as key players. My colleagues and I recently identified a gene linked to altruistic(利他的) behavior and found that a particular variant of it was associated with more selfish behavior in preschoolers. According to evolutionary scientists, cooperative behavior may have evolved first among relatives to promote the continuation of their genetic line. As communities diversified, mutual support could have broadened to include individuals not linked by blood. Another possibility is that humans cooperate to gain some advantage, such as boosting reputation. Finally, evolutionary processes take place at the group level. Groups of highly cooperative individuals have higher chances of survival because they can work together to reach goals that are unattainable to less cooperative groups. Yet almost no behavior is entirely genetic, even among identical twins. Culture, schooling and parenting are important determinants of cooperation. Thus, the degree to which we act cooperatively or selfishly is unique to each individual and depends on a variety of genetic and environmental influences.

questions.s: What is the finding of one recent study about being selfish?

o.t: It may bring certain benefits in the short term.
It usually yields more disadvantages than advantages.
It serves individual interest rather than a collective's.

translation.source: 中国有句老话："一日为师，终身为父"。在中国人的观念里，老师不仅传授知识，更教给学生做人的道 理。在古代，学生初次见老师时要举行隆重的仪式，足见老师地位之高。为弘扬尊师的优良传统，中国从1985 年开始将每年的9月10日定为教师节。在这一天，学生以各种方式表达对老师的敬意。尊师是中华民族的传统 美德，在当今社会得到了发扬光大。
translation.reference: There is an old Chinese saying: "A teacher for a day is a father for a lifetime." In the eyes of Chinese people, teachers not only impart knowledge, but also teach students how to be a good person. In ancient times, students had to hold a grand ceremony when they met their teacher for the first time, which was enough to show the high status of teachers. To carry forward the fine tradition of respecting teachers, China has observed September 10 of each year as Teachers' Day since 1985. On this day, students express their respect for teachers in various ways. Respecting teachers is a traditional virtue of the Chinese nation, and it has been carried forward in today's society.
